t1487.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Ḥammād ibn Usāma, Abū Usāma al-Kūfī, as reliable and firm, sometimes practicing tadlīs and in later years narrating from others' books; one of the senior ninth generation, he died in 201 at eighty.
as: ثقة ثبت ربما دلس وكان بأخرة يحدث من كتب غيره
Reliable and firm, though he sometimes practiced tadlīs, and in his later years would narrate from others' books.
Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, quoted by al-Mizzī
أبو أسامة ثقة، كان أعلم الناس بأمور الناس، وأخبار أهل الكوفة، وما كان أرواه عن هشام بن عروة!
Abū Usāmah was trustworthy, exceptionally knowledgeable about people and the reports of Kufans, and a prolific transmitter from Hishām ibn ʿUrwah.
Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn, quoted by al-Mizzī
Ibn Maʿīn says both Abū Usāmah and ʿAbdah are trustworthy.
محمد بن عبد الله بن عمار الموصلي, quoted by al-Mizzī
كان أبو أسامة في زمن سفيان يعد من النساك.
In Sufyān’s time, Abū Usāmah was counted among the devout.
ما بالكوفة شاب أعقل من أبي أسامة.
There is no young man in Kufa more sensible than Abū Usāmah.
وكان ثقة مأمونا كثير الحديث يدلس وتبين تدليسه. وكان صاحب سنة وجماعة.
He was trustworthy and reliable, prolific in hadith, and practiced tadlīs, which became apparent. He adhered to the Sunnah and the community.

t1982.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Zāʾida ibn Qudāma al-Thaqafī, Abū al-Ṣalt al-Kūfī, as trustworthy, firm, and a man of Sunnah, of the seventh generation; he died in 160 AH, it is said, or later.
as: trustworthy, firm, a man of Sunnah
عليك بزائدة بن قدامة، وسفيان بن عيينة
He recommended hearing hadith from Zāʾidah ibn Qudāmah and Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah.
حدثنا زائدة وكان من أصدق الناس وإبره
Zāʾidah transmitted to us. He was among the most truthful and upright.
أبو داود الطيالسي, quoted by al-Mizzī
حدثنا زائدة بن قدامة، وكان لا يحدث قدريا ولا صاحب بدعة يعرفه
Zāʾidah transmitted to us. He refused to transmit to Qadarīs and people he knew to hold innovations.
Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, quoted by al-Mizzī
المتثبتون في الحديث أربعة: سفيان، وشعبة، وزهير، وزائدة
Four were exacting in verifying hadith: Sufyān, Shuʿbah, Zuhayr, and Zāʾidah.
Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, quoted by al-Mizzī
إذا سمعت الحديث، عن زائدة وزهير فلا تبال ألا تسمعه عن غيرهما إلا حديث أبي إسحاق
If you hear a hadith from Zāʾidah and Zuhayr, you need not hear it from anyone else, except for the hadith of Abū Isḥāq.
Abū Zurʿah al-Rāzī, quoted by al-Mizzī
Truthful and one of the learned.
Abū Ḥātim al-Rāzī, quoted by al-Mizzī
كان ثقة، صاحب سنة، وهو أحب إلي من أبي عوانة وأحفظ من شريك، وأبي بكر بن عياش، وكان عرض حديثه على سفيان الثوري
Reliable and a follower of the Sunnah. I prefer him to Abū ʿAwānah, and he had a better memory than Sharīk and Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh. He presented his hadith to Sufyān al-Thawrī.
كان ثقة، صاحب سنة، لا يحدث أحدا حتى يسأل عنه، فإن كان صاحب سنة حدثه وإلا لم يحدثه
Reliable and a follower of the Sunnah. He would ask about a prospective student and only teach those who followed the Sunnah.
وكان زائدة ثقة مأمونا صاحب سنة وجماعة
Zāʾidah was reliable, trustworthy, and a follower of the Sunnah and the community.

t402.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Asʿad ibn Sahl ibn Ḥunayf al-Anṣārī, Abū Umāma, counted among the Companions, who saw the Prophet but did not hear from him, and died in 100 aged ninety-two.
as: Abū Zurʿah al-Rāzī, quoted by Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī
وأنكر أبو زرعة سماعه من عمر
Abū Zurʿah denied that he heard from ʿUmar.
al-Bukhārī, quoted by Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī
أدرك النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ولم يسمع منه
He lived in the Prophet’s lifetime but did not hear from him.
البغوي, quoted by Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī
أدرك النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ولم يسمع منه
He lived in the Prophet’s lifetime but did not hear from him.
ابن السكن, quoted by Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī
أدرك النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ولم يسمع منه
He lived in the Prophet’s lifetime but did not hear from him.
Ibn Ḥibbān, quoted by Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī
أدرك النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ولم يسمع منه
He lived in the Prophet’s lifetime but did not hear from him.
ابن أبو داود, quoted by Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī
صحب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وبايعه
He accompanied the Prophet and pledged allegiance to him.
ابن مندة, quoted by Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī
الباوردي, quoted by Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī
مختلف في صحبته، إلا أنه ولد في عهد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
His Companionship is disputed, although he was born in the Prophet’s lifetime.
الطبراني, quoted by Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī
وهو أحد الجلة من العلماء من كبار التابعين بالمدينة، ولم يسمع من النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم شيئا ولا صحبه
A distinguished scholar among Medina’s senior Successors. He did not accompany or hear from the Prophet.
He was one of the leading scholars.
ابن أبو داود, quoted by Ibn al-Athīr
صحب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وبايعه وبارك عليه وحنكه
He accompanied and pledged allegiance to the Prophet, who blessed him and performed taḥnīk.
He was trustworthy and narrated many hadiths.

t6598.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Musaddad ibn Musarhad al-Asadī, Abū al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī, as trustworthy and a memorizer, of the tenth generation; he died in 28 AH. It is said he was the first to compile the Musnad in Basra, and that his name was ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, Musaddad being a nickname.
as: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd al-Qaṭṭān, quoted by al-Mizzī
لو أتيت مسددا فحدثته في بيته لكان يستأهل
If I went to Musaddad and narrated to him in his house, he would deserve it.
Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, quoted by al-Mizzī
مسدد صدوق، فما كتبته عنه فلا تعده
Musaddad is truthful; what you have written from him, do not repeat.
أبو عبد الله, quoted by al-Mizzī
What an excellent shaykh, may God keep him well.
Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn, quoted by al-Mizzī
Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn, quoted by al-Mizzī
اكتب عن مسدد فإنه ثقة ثقة
Write from Musaddad, for he is reliable, reliable.
Abū Ḥātim al-Rāzī, quoted by al-Mizzī
أبو حاتم الرازي, quoted by al-Mizzī
كأنها الدنانير، ثم قال: كأنك تسمعها من النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
Of his hadith from Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd: they are like gold dinars; it is as if you hear them from the Prophet.

t8563.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Ḥafṣa bint ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, Mother of the Believers. The Prophet married her after Khunays ibn Ḥudhāfa in the year 3, and she died in the year 45.

t8761.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Umm Kulthūm al-Laythiyyah al-Makkiyyah, said to be the daughter of Muḥammad ibn Abī Bakr al-Ṣiddīq (thus Taimī not Laythī), with a hadith from ʿĀʾishah narrated by ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr.

t929.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Jaʿdah al-Makhzūmī, from the descendants of Umm Hānī, said to be the son of Yaḥyā ibn Jaʿdah ibn Hubayrah, as maqbūl, of the sixth generation.
